title: prefill/decode: chunked speculative prefill + stage-overlap optimizations + kernel scheduler improvements
author: Riley Chen
description:
Context and motivation: We continue to optimize end-to-end inference latency and throughput for mixed prefill+decode workloads. Customers running chat-style traffic see a wide distribution of prefill lengths (short prompts to multi-turn histories) and decode lengths. Previous work introduced stage overlap (prefill and decode concurrency) and speculative prefill; this PR combines chunked prefill, improved speculative prefill heuristics, tighter KV-cache integration, and a kernel-aware scheduler to better utilize GPU kernels and reduce tail latency.

Summary of changes:
- Introduce chunked prefill execution path that splits long prefill sequences into configurable chunks, enabling earlier decode progress and better KV memory locality.
- Extend speculative prefill to be chunk-aware: speculative token generation for decode can begin as soon as the first prefill chunk completes, with rollback/merge semantics when subsequent chunks arrive.
- Implement stage-overlap orchestrator in runtime/pipeline that coordinates prefill chunk streaming, KV cache warming, and decode token handoff.
- Add kernel_scheduler component that ranks available kernels by per-batch expected latency (taking into account sequence length distribution and kv-cache hit-rate) and pins short sequences to low-latency kernels while batching long sequences on high-throughput kernels.
- Tighten KV cache lifecycles and prefetch heuristics to reduce cache thrash during chunked prefill; add async prefetch for upcoming chunks.
- Continuous-batching improvements: allow dynamic batch cutpoints based on kernel selection decisions and stage overlap signals.
- Tests and benchmarks: new microbench harness and end-to-end perf tests covering short/long prefill mixes and high concurrency.

Design notes:
- Chunk size defaults to 64 tokens (configurable per model/profile). Prefill stages emit partial KV checkpoints after each chunk; these are mergeable to reconstruct a full prefill state.
- Speculative prefill uses probabilistic confidence thresholds (derived from language-model token probabilities) to decide how many speculative tokens to synthesize early. On mis-speculation we perform deterministic re-decode and merge partial outputs; cost of mis-speculation is bounded by re-decode of a short window.
- Kernel scheduler collects lightweight telemetry (seq_len, kv_hits, recent kernel latency) per worker and computes a score to select kernel variant for a batch. This minimizes kernel warmup penalties and reduces per-token median latency for small sequences.
- KV cache prefetch triggers on expected next-chunk ranges and on speculative decode warm-starts; eviction policy gives short-lived prefill checkpoints a slightly higher priority to avoid re-compute on common chat flows.

Commits (high-level):
- Add chunked prefill pipeline and prefill checkpoint format (runtime/prefill/*)
- Implement chunk-aware speculative prefill and rollback/merge semantics
- Add kernel_scheduler and integrate with batch router
- KV cache prefetch/eviction improvements and tests
- Continuous-batching: dynamic cutpoints and config knobs
- Add perf harness and end-to-end benchmarks; fix follow-up test flakes

Review conversation (selected comments):
- Maya Patel: "Nice end-to-end design. Can you add a small diagram to docs/observability showing chunk checkpoints and decode handoff? Also please call out the default chunk size in the config docs."
- Riley Chen (author): "Added docs/observability/prefill_metrics.md with diagram and default config note; updated examples to surface chunk_size."
- Aaron Chen: "Benchmarks look promising. In kernel_scheduler, should we add a hard cap on switching kernels to avoid thrash? Also the scheduling logic looks a bit heavy for the fast path; can we opportunistically sample?"
- Riley Chen: "Good points. Added a sticky-kernel policy with a short TTL (configurable) and switched to sampled telemetry on the fast path. See kernel_scheduler.cpp lines ~120-220 for the sampling implementation."
- Pavel Orlov: "Behavioral question: on mis-speculative prefill, what's the observable behavior for clients? Any OOE (out-of-order events) risk for streaming consumers?"
- Riley Chen: "Mis-speculation triggers a short re-decode; we emit a corrective patch token stream using the established delta-append API so streaming clients see a correction rather than an abrupt replacement. Documented in the design notes and unit tests assert the patch semantics."
- Lina Gomez: "Please ensure CI covers both short-prefill-heavy and long-prefill-heavy workloads; also add a canary rollout plan (10% of traffic with metrics rollback)."
- Riley Chen: "Added perf tests and a rollout plan to the PR description; ops has a canary job ready."

release_notes: chunked prefill + stage-overlap and kernel scheduler improvements reduce median latency ~11% and increase throughput ~6% for mixed prefill/decode workloads; configurable knobs added for chunking/speculation/kernel-sticky policies.
canary_plan: 10% traffic for 48h with automated rollback on >3% median or >5% p95 regressions; dashboards and alerts already configured.
notes: No breaking changes. Feature is opt-in for Dedicated/Private by default. Observability docs and examples included.
